content.title: Arvada Real Time Information Center (ARTIC)
content.summary: The Arvada Real Time Information Center (ARTIC), located in City Hall, utilizes advanced technology to enhance public safety and city operations by providing real-time information to staff across various departments. It integrates tools such as live camera feeds, drone technology, and data analysis to improve response times and decision-making during emergencies, while ensuring compliance with legal standards and protecting privacy rights. Community engagement has been prioritized through meetings and transparency initiatives, including regular updates on ARTIC's activities and contributions.
content.body:
## Overview

Located on the second floor of City Hall in the former Arvada PD Communications Center, the Arvada Real Time Information Center (ARTIC) is designed to use technology to support not just public safety, but operations across the entire City organization. The goal is simple: give staff better information, sooner, so they can make better decisions in real time.

While real-time information/crime centers were first developed for policing, Arvada’s approach is broader. Fully realized, the ARTIC will bring together live camera feeds, drone technology, and other data sources to support Departments ranging from police and fire to utilities, streets, engineering, and parks.

## ARTIC Video Presentation

Arvada PD hosted three community meetings to educate residents and hear feedback, questions, and concerns about the ARTIC. Community members can watch a [recorded version of the presentation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cvOFW039iUs) that was shown at the meetings.

## What ARTIC Does

ARTIC technicians use a combination of technology and data sources to support public safety and City operations, including:

- Monitoring calls for service in real time
- Assisting officers with critical information during active incidents
- Supporting investigations with data analysis and video review
- Coordinating information from various systems to improve response

### Technology Integration

ARTIC brings together multiple tools into one coordinated system, including:

- Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) software
- City owned camera systems
- Drone First Responder (DFR)
- Automated license plate reader (ALPR) data
- Law enforcement and open source databases

This integration allows for faster, more informed decision-making in the field.

### Public Safety Benefits

- Improved response times through real-time intelligence
- Enhanced officer and community safety
- More efficient allocation of resources
- Better coordination during emergencies and large-scale incidents

### Safeguards and Oversight

- All technology used by the Department complies with state and federal law, Department policy, and policing best practices
- Access to systems is restricted to authorized personnel
- Data may only be used for legitimate law enforcement purposes
- Activity is logged, monitored, and subject to audit

## ARTIC Data & Transparency

This section will include regularly updated statistics, such as:

- Number of incidents supported
- Types of calls assisted
- Use of drone deployments
- Investigative contributions

## ARTIC FAQs

### What is the ARTIC?

The Arvada Real Time Information Center (ARTIC) is a centralized hub where trained staff use technology and data to support police and City operations in real time. It enhances situational awareness, improves response times, and provides officers and investigators with timely, actionable information.

### What does the ARTIC do on a daily basis?

ARTIC technicians monitor camera systems, deploy drones when appropriate, and analyze available data to support calls for service, active incidents, and ongoing investigations. They provide officers with real-time updates that help them make informed decisions in the field.

### What types of technology are used in the ARTIC?

The ARTIC integrates several tools, including:

- City owned camera systems
- Drone First Responder (DFR) technology
- Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) data and systems
- Computer-aided dispatch (CAD) information
- Records and analytical tools

All technology is used in compliance with laws and Department policies.

### Is the ARTIC surveilling people in real time?

No. The ARTIC is not used for random or continuous surveillance of individuals. It is a response-driven system, meaning staff use technology to support active calls, investigations, and public safety needs, not to monitor people without a legitimate law enforcement purpose.

### How are privacy and civil liberties protected?

All ARTIC operations are governed by strict policies, laws, and auditing processes. Access to systems is limited to trained personnel, and all use must be tied to a legitimate law enforcement purpose. Misuse of any system can result in disciplinary action and potential criminal charges.

### Does the ARTIC store or share data?

Data access and retention is dependent on the specific system being used and the associated laws and policies related to the type of data. The City of Arvada maintains ownership of its data and strictly regulates who can access it. Information is only shared with authorized law enforcement partners when legally permitted and for legitimate investigative purposes.

### Can the ARTIC be used during emergencies?

Yes. The ARTIC plays a key role during critical incidents, including major crimes, missing persons cases, fires, and natural disasters. It supports coordination between responding units and can provide real-time intelligence to improve decision-making.

### Are drones always being used or flying over the city?

No. Drones are deployed on a case-by-case basis to support specific incidents. Their use is governed by FAA regulations and Department policy, and they are not used for routine or continuous patrol.

### How does the ARTIC support investigations?

ARTIC staff can quickly gather and analyze information from multiple systems, helping detectives identify leads, track suspect vehicles, and piece together timelines more efficiently.

### Will ARTIC activity and statistics be shared publicly?

Yes. The Department is committed to transparency and will provide regular updates, including monthly statistics and examples of how the ARTIC supports public safety efforts.

### How can the public learn more or ask questions?

Community members are encouraged to watch the ARTIC presentation video available on this page. Feedback and questions are always welcome as the Department works to maintain transparency and build community trust. You can contact us about the ARTIC by emailing [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#dabba8acbbbebbaab5b6b3b9bfaab3b59abba8acbbbebbf4b5a8bd), submitting a question through [AskArvada](https://www.arvadaco.gov/898/Report-a-Problem-or-Ask-a-Question), or calling (303) 980-7300.

## Commitment to Transparency

ARTIC reflects the Department’s commitment to using technology thoughtfully and responsibly. By combining innovation with clear policies and oversight, ARTIC helps improve public safety while maintaining community trust.
